00247.source_location: NCCP 00247 v5 pp. 1–2; HSE GTD guideline v2 pp. 49–50.
00247.patient_question: Why do I still have appointments after my hormone level returns to normal?
00247.patient_answer: The first normal blood result is a milestone. Three more cycles help clear any remaining disease. Ask your specialist nurse to write down your last treatment date, your next blood test and who will give you the result.
00247.clinician_update: Agree the consolidation appointments and designate a contact for the transition to surveillance. Record the first normal hCG, end of consolidation and first follow-up blood test separately.
00247.assessment_scope: Post-methotrexate hCG below, equal to and above 1,000 IU/L. An IV-site symptom and its negative control. The source does not assign equality to the less-than indication.

00248.source_location: NCCP 00248 v5 p. 6, methotrexate respiratory toxicity.
00248.patient_question: Should I call about a dry cough between visits?
00248.patient_answer: Phone your 24-hour oncology number straight away for a persistent dry cough or new breathlessness. Methotrexate can cause lung inflammation, and infection can cause similar symptoms. Your team needs to assess you even if you have no fever.
00248.clinician_update: Ask about persistent dry cough, new dyspnoea and fever at each review. Consider methotrexate pneumonitis alongside infection and assess promptly.
00248.assessment_scope: Day 8 cyclophosphamide at creatinine clearance 9.9 and 10 mL/min, with an EMA visit control. Grade 3 neuropathy during the vincristine visit and a non-vincristine visit.

00249.source_location: NCCP 00249 v4 p. 1, treatment and administration table.
00249.patient_question: How do my spinal treatment and my other chemotherapy fit together?
00249.patient_answer: Ask the team to put the spinal appointment, your other chemotherapy and each rescue tablet on one dated plan. Before leaving, check which tablet is due 24 hours after the spinal treatment. If two sets of instructions overlap, call the unit before taking an extra tablet.
00249.clinician_update: Reconcile the three spinal doses with systemic therapy and all folinic acid orders. In low-risk GTN with lung metastases they accompany the first three methotrexate courses. In high-risk GTN they usually accompany the EMA block. Provide one reconciled rescue timetable.
00249.assessment_scope: Two versus three preceding spinal doses, a rescue-only visit control, and methotrexate renal caution at creatinine clearance 29.9 versus 30 mL/min.

00264.source_location: NCCP 00264 v4 pp. 2 and 5, hydration and cisplatin toxicities.
00264.patient_question: What if I cannot keep fluids down after the day 8 infusion?
00264.patient_answer: Call your 24-hour oncology number promptly if vomiting prevents you from drinking or you are passing less urine. Cisplatin can strain the kidneys. Tell the team when you last drank and passed urine so they can assess whether you need fluids through a drip.
00264.clinician_update: On the day 8 cisplatin visit, check ability to maintain oral hydration. If nausea or vomiting precludes it, assess for IV hydration. Review concurrent nephrotoxic medicines and check for hearing or sensory changes before each cisplatin cycle.
00264.assessment_scope: Cisplatin renal decisions at 44.9, 45 and 59.5 mL/min, an EMA visit control and grade 2 neuropathy during EP. Values outside the printed cisplatin bands require review.

00266.source_location: NCCP 00266 v5 pp. 1–4, schedule, exclusions and toxicity modifications.
00266.patient_question: Why should I report tingling or ringing in my ears before the next visit?
00266.patient_answer: Paclitaxel is given at both visits. Cisplatin is given on day 1 and can affect hearing and nerves. Tell your team about ringing, changes in hearing, numb fingers or difficulty fastening buttons so they can check which medicine needs review.
00266.clinician_update: Record hearing symptoms and functional sensory changes against the actual visit. Both TP and TE contain paclitaxel. Cisplatin is present only on day 1. Distinguish baseline cisplatin exclusions from toxicity first detected during treatment.
00266.assessment_scope: Baseline grade 1 versus grade 2 neuropathy during TP, an on-treatment control and significant hearing symptoms at the cisplatin versus non-cisplatin visit.
